learning_outcomes.text: Identify questions of an optimization nature in order to construct mathematical models for simpler optimization problems.
Use the basic concepts and theorems described by the course content, as well as choose and apply appropriate methods in order to solve commonly occurring optimization problems.
Argue for their approaches using relevant concepts within the course, and present clear calculations and reasoning.
Use available optimization software to solve standard optimization problems.

syllabus_topics: General optimality concepts: Basic convexity theory for functions and sets, optimality conditions, local and global optima, relaxation and restriction.
Linear programming: Linear optimization models with continuous decision variables, graphical solution, mathematical theory of linear programming, the simplex method, duality, sensitivity analysis.

Nonlinear programming: Nonlinear optimization models continuous decision variables, with/without subconditions, steepest slope method, Newton's (modified) method, exact line search, interval bisection, the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions.
teaching_methods: Lectures (including theory, problem solving and applications)
Laboratory course (with emphasis on modelling and the use of optimization software)
assessment_rules: Grades for examination modules are decided in accordance with the assessment criteria presented at the start of the course. The grading scale is U, 3, 4, 5.
